answer_1.quote: The most common procedure in neural machine translation (NMT) is to train models using maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) at training time, and to decode with beam search at test time, as a way to approximate maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) decoding.

answer_2.quote: We evaluate each system using the metrics discussed in §3.1, along with BLEU and chrF.

answer_4.quote: We perform a human-study to more faithfully evaluate our systems ... We ask annotators to rate, from 1 (no overlap in meaning) to 5 (perfect translation), the translations ... and ... we perform another human study, this time based on expert-level multidimensional quality metrics (MQM) annotations. We asked the annotators to identify all errors and independently label them with an error category (accuracy, fluency, and style, each with a specific set of subcategories) and a severity level (minor, major, and critical).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated translations on a 1-5 scale for meaning overlap and identified errors with categories (accuracy, fluency, style) and severity levels (minor, major, critical).
